slides.highlight: The development of a humanoid robot featuring lifelike skin and emotional AI is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Chinese Tech Firm Unveils Robot Companion
slides.highlight: The introduction of a robot companion sparks debate on technological progress versus its impact on real-life relationships, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
slides.highlight: This research introduces ConsumerSim, a generative framework that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics using synthetic populations and behavioral signals, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: ConsumerSim reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics as a salience-driven response process between heterogeneous agents and environments.
card.key_idea: A generative framework using microdata-calibrated synthetic populations, situational signal fields, and behavioral inertia alignment to simulate how diverse households respond to salient economic shocks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on U.S., EU27, and Japan CCI series against 14 baselines; outperformed them in MAE/RMSE and improved short-horizon housing activity predictions.
card.limitation: Relies on external signal quality, uses agents as imperfect cognitive proxies, and lacks full local population substrates for non-U.S. regions.

slides.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
slides.tldr: SCALING LLMS IMPROVES SOCIAL SIMULATION FIDELITY
slides.highlight: This research examines how compute scaling affects the fidelity of LLM-based social simulations, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Scaling compute generally improves LLM social simulation, but fails for specific cognitive biases and underrepresented populations.
card.key_idea: The authors used compute-scaling laws (85 Qwen3 models) and observational laws (35 open-weight models) to analyze opinion, behavior, and longitudinal simulations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using World Values Survey, Psych-101, and ACL datasets. Results show log-linear scaling for most tasks, though some behavioral tasks remain orthogonal.
card.limitation: Scaling fails to improve calibration for human cognitive biases (e.g., risk aversion) and low-resource demographic domains.

slides.title: TurnNat: Automatic Evaluation of Turn-Taking Naturalness in Dyadic Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: TurnNat provides a likelihood-based framework to automatically evaluate turn-taking naturalness in spoken dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and team state.

card.one_liner: TurnNat automatically evaluates turn-taking naturalness using a likelihood-based framework for two-channel spoken dialogue.
card.key_idea: A causal model predicts future two-speaker voice-activity states; negative log-likelihood (NLL) aggregated over turn-taking boundary units (TBUs) measures timing atypicality to score conversational naturalness.
card.evaluation: Tested on a human-validated perturbation benchmark (Seamless Interaction dataset) using C-index and pairwise accuracy. Best model achieved 88.0% matched-pair accuracy.
card.limitation: Evaluates controlled perturbations of human dialogue; may miss failures related to ASR, semantics, prosody, or specific task contexts.

slides.title: LLM-Powered Interactive Robotic Action Synthesis from Multimodal Speech, Gestures, and Music
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to synthesize robotic actions from speech, gestures, and music, advancing fluid and context-aware human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework using LLMs to synthesize quadruped robot actions from speech, hand gestures, and music beats.
card.key_idea: Integrates Whisper (speech), gesture recognition, and beat detection into structured prompts for a Qwen3:0.6b LLM to map multimodal inputs to a predefined robot action space.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot via preliminary experiments; demonstrated successful execution of a handstand triggered by gestures and rhythmic beats.
card.limitation: Relies on a constrained action space of pre-vetted skills and requires further optimization for real-time responsiveness.

slides.title: Reference-Based Prosody and Rhythm Evaluation for Spoken Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This work introduces a percentile-based evaluation protocol for conversational prosody and rhythm, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A reference-based evaluation protocol for assessing prosody and rhythm plausibility in speech-to-speech AI agents.
card.key_idea: Uses 4,000+ hours of conversational speech to create matched reference strata based on sex, age, arousal, and dominance for percentile-based behavioral plausibility checks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on held-out human data; matched references correctly flagged ~10% of rows, whereas pooled references over-flagged state-conditioned expressivity and rhythm.
card.limitation: Based on a single English corpus; uses model-predicted traits instead of ground-truth metadata; does not map deviations to perceptual naturalness.

slides.title: From Technical Metrics to User Perception: A User Study of a Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction System for Object Detection and Grasping
slides.tldr: USER PERCEPTION OF MULTIMODAL HRI IMPROVEMENTS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that technical gains in object-grasping success rates are perceptible to users, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction through user-centered evidence.

card.one_liner: A user study confirms that a 15% technical success gain in a robot grasping system is perceptible.
card.key_idea: Compared a baseline HRI system (Florence-2, LLaMA 3.1) against an improved version (Grounding DINO+SAM, Qwen 3.5 9B) using a within-subject user study on object grasping.
card.evaluation: 24 participants rated speed, reliability, and competence via 7-point Likert scales. Results showed significant preference and higher ratings for the improved system (p < 0.05).
card.limitation: The improved system still exhibited occasional failures, leaving users perceiving it as not fully dependable for real-world deployment.

slides.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
slides.highlight: This work introduces SenseWalk, which combines LLMs and the social force model to simulate human movement patterns and semantic trajectories, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SenseWalk is an interactive system for simulating physically plausible and semantically coherent human trajectories in zoned environments.
card.key_idea: A hybrid workflow combining LLM-powered agents for high-level semantic planning and the social force model for low-level physical movement constraints.
card.evaluation: Quantitative experiments across four real-world venue models using physical and semantic loss metrics, plus a user study with 12 participants.

slides.title: Automatic Detection of Stress from Speech in the Trier Social Stress Test
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates the use of speaker diarization and acoustic-prosodic features to automatically detect stress responses, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of human states.

card.one_liner: Speech-based machine learning can automatically distinguish stressful from non-stressful situations and predict specific stress responses.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using speaker diarization and ML models (XGBoost, SVR, RF) analyzed 144 acoustic-prosodic features to classify TSST vs. f-TSST and predict cortisol and affect.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 50 participants using nested cross-validation. XGBoost achieved 82% accuracy; SVR and XGB outperformed baselines in predicting cortisol and negative affect.
card.limitation: Protocol-related cues in the TSST/f-TSST contrast may influence results, and sAA reactivity could not be consistently predicted.

slides.title: HABIT: Human-Aware Behavior and Interaction Training Dataset for Robot Manipulation
slides.highlight: The HABIT dataset provides large-scale demonstrations of human-robot interaction across collaborator, coworker, and supervisor roles, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: HABIT is a large-scale robot demonstration dataset designed to teach robots human-aware behaviors in shared workspaces.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 10K+ episodes across 60 tasks, categorized by human roles: Collaborator (joint tasks), Coworker (shared space), and Supervisor (human-directed cues).
card.evaluation: Fine-tuned $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.6 models; compared against robot-only baselines using success rates, workflow compliance, and safety metrics across six tasks.
card.limitation: Collected in a single environment with ten operators, limiting diversity in body silhouettes, motion styles, and multi-agent dynamics.

slides.title: Investigating LLM-Powered Dissenting Minority Support in Power-Imbalanced Group Decision-Making: Counterargument and Mediation as Intervention Strategies
slides.tldr: LLM-POWERED SUPPORT FOR MINORITY VIEWS IN GROUP DECISIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores how AI-generated counterarguments and mediated messages affect group dynamics and minority participation in power-imbalanced settings, contributing to HyECHO's focus on group norms and engagement.

card.one_liner: AI-generated counterarguments improve group atmosphere, but AI-mediated minority revoicing paradoxically reduces psychological safety.
card.key_idea: An LLM system supporting minorities via either autonomous counterarguments (AIGC) or paraphrasing private minority dissent as AI-authored messages (AIMM) to mask authorship in power-imbalanced groups.
card.evaluation: Mixed-method experiment with 96 participants (24 groups) using role-playing (Seniors vs. Juniors) to simulate power imbalance and compliance pressure.
card.limitation: Revoicing-based interventions may unintentionally intensify marginalization by discounting human agency or obscuring authentic dissent in hierarchical settings.

slides.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL SPEAKER RECOGNITION IN LONG-FORM VIDEO
slides.highlight: This work introduces DramaSR-LRM and a large-scale benchmark to improve speaker attribution by synthesizing auditory, linguistic, and visual cues. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization within complex social contexts.

card.one_liner: A reasoning LLM framework and large-scale benchmark for attributing spoken utterances to characters in TV dramas.
card.key_idea: DramaSR-LRM uses a Qwen3-8B backbone fine-tuned via SFT and GRPO to synthesize voiceprint similarity, video captioning, and character relationship tools.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DramaSR-532K (532K utterances, 11 test dramas) against label propagation and pyannote; accuracy improved from 85.49% to 87.79%.
card.limitation: Relies on a spatiotemporal neighborhood assumption for candidate selection, which may struggle with off-screen narration or low-visibility scenes.

slides.title: Adaptive Companionship for Group-Following Robots: Handling Dynamically Changing Group Formations
slides.highlight: This work utilizes Vision-Language Models to infer group dynamics and companion positions, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A VLM-based method for robots to adaptively accompany human groups with dynamic membership and formations.
card.key_idea: Combines a VLM for semantic reasoning over a grid-based interaction space with an MPPI-CBF controller for stable, safe, and socially appropriate group-following.
card.evaluation: Tested across five scenarios and a 20-person user study; showed 15% higher success rate and 25% lower collision rate than baselines.
card.limitation: Performance and latency degrade as group size increases, with significant success rate drops for groups of 12 members.
